tagline: Two roads, one lagoon, and a treasure fleet just offshore.
intro: The highway is two roads with the Indian River Lagoon between them, A1A out on the barrier island along the Atlantic and US 1 on the mainland through Fort Pierce and Port St. Lucie, with Fort Pierce at the center. The view runs from the coastal dunes across to the mangrove banks of a lagoon 156 miles long, home to more than 4,300 species, manatees and sea turtles among them.
In 1715 a hurricane drove a Spanish fleet carrying gold and some 14 million pesos of silver onto this coast. More than half of its 2,000 men died.

moments.title: Urca de Lima
moments.text: Two hundred yards off Jack Island Park lies a 1715 cargo ship the Spanish burned to the waterline to hide it from pirates, now Florida's first underwater archaeological preserve.

moments.title: National Navy UDT-SEAL Museum
moments.text: The original Navy frogmen first trained just outside Fort Pierce, and the museum keeps the obstacles they practiced demolishing before Normandy and the spacecraft trainers they used to rehearse astronaut recoveries.

moments.title: Douglass Beach
moments.text: Just offshore, in water never more than about 20 feet deep, coins from the 1715 fleet lie above a drowned stretch of old dry land holding Pleistocene horse bones and 4,800-year-old pottery.
